title: Trishakti Industries Ltd - 531279 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Trishakti Q1 FY27 total income up ~310% YoY to INR 1,680 lakh, EBITDA ~INR 1,087 lakh at ~65% margin, PAT INR 430 lakh.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR 1,680 lakh (up nearly 310% YoY), EBITDA of INR 1,087 lakh (about four times YoY, ~65% margin), PBT of INR 538 lakh and PAT of INR 430 lakh, described as the strongest quarter in company history. Fleet utilisation was stated at 100% with fleet of roughly 155-158 machines. Management announced entry into wind energy equipment rental (900-ton cranes) and intent to expand into UAE and KSA, both subject to approvals. Executable order book for FY27 was put at INR 70-72 crore, with management saying signed contracts cover the full financial year.

segments.name: Crane / equipment rental (India core)
segments.commentary: Fleet of roughly 155-158 machines at 100% utilisation; FY27 executable order book INR 70-72 crore, with management guiding ~60% EBITDA and 25-30% PAT margin on that book. Management said payments from core business are received within 60 days.

segments.name: Wind energy equipment rental (new)
segments.commentary: Entry announced with 900-ton machines; first units expected in India in October; management expects revenue contribution in Q3-Q4 FY27 and yields similar to current fleet. No order book disclosed yet; 2-3 month advance LOIs referenced as possible.

segments.name: Tower cranes for data centres (new)
segments.commentary: Management disclosed two new machine types including 80-ton tower cranes for data-centre jobs; about INR 100 crore of CapEx placed for these and other machines, expected live in four to five months.

segments.name: UAE and KSA (planned)
segments.commentary: Planned entry via incorporation of new entities; management cited ~50-52% EBITDA margin expectation in KSA and yields of ~4% per month versus ~2.5% in India. Deployment targeted within two to three quarters; no roadmap or CapEx quantum given yet.

guidance_outlook: FY27 executable order book INR 70-72 crore, expected to deliver ~60% EBITDA and 25-30% PAT margin; revenue to rise as new machines start earning (~1.5 month lead time).
FY27 CapEx plan of INR 400 crore: ~INR 270 crore done, balance INR 130-140 crore to be spent in India in FY27; ~70% of balance already ordered per management.
Margins expected to normalise to 58-62% EBITDA once OEM warranty (about three years) ends and maintenance OpEx of 4-5% of top line starts.
Management expects utilisation to stay above 95-98%; fleet utilisation expected in the 90s after geographic diversification.
Borrowing cost expected to fall over the next few quarters as legacy 9.75% loans are repaid.
Management declined to give FY28 estimates; said a fuller roadmap would come in the December quarter call.
capex_capacity: Cumulative gross block: ~INR 270 crore per management; ~INR 235-240 crore excluding GST, per balance sheet comments.
FY26 CapEx was INR 210 crore against a guidance of INR 100 crore.

Wind energy 900-ton machines: 4-5 units could absorb the remaining INR 130 crore; OEM lead time about four months plus transport, ~5 months net; OEM output of ~2-5 machines per month cited as constraint.
Electric (EV) machines: ordered for two clients, ~2-month lead time, ~5% costlier than diesel units, expected in Q2 FY27.
UAE/KSA CapEx: no quantum given; management said a roadmap would follow once client demand data is collected by next month-end.
demand_pricing: Management says demand in India is strong, with post-monsoon mega-projects (including Reliance Kutch expansion) expected from October.
Client yields in India cited at ~2.5% per month; KSA yields cited at ~4% per month; KSA EBITDA margin expectation 50-52%.
Customers named: L&T, KEC, Afcon, Reliance; wind EPC players referred to as potential partners (names not given).
Management said the client bears diesel cost; Trishakti bears operator, helper and labour accommodation costs.
Competition: management said peers such as Sanghvi and Barker face supply constraints; no pricing data given. Wind market entry barriers cited as CapEx scale and OEM capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Current fleet size and wind energy segment economics, payback and order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Fleet 155-158 machines. Wind yields said to be similar to the current fleet; no existing wind client base; talks with large wind EPC companies; no payback figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Funding model for new cranes and debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: Banks now fund ~100% of machine cost (previously 20% down payment), with LTV ~50-60%; borrowings ~INR 80-85 crore; average cost ~8.5-8.75%; interest paid from month one with moratorium.

qa_highlights.question: Debtor days, reported around 200 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said core-business receipts are under 60 days and expects debtor days to fall to 60-70 in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is utilisation and EBITDA better than peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Fleet is 2024-2027 vintage versus peers' 12-15 years; OEM covers maintenance for first three years; margin expected to fall to 58-62% later.

qa_highlights.question: Why expand into UAE and KSA, and what is the right to win?
qa_highlights.answer: Clients (L&T, KEC, Afcon, Reliance) asked for support abroad; KSA yields higher; management said it will target specific clients rather than compete on fleet size with peers such as Sanghvi.

qa_highlights.question: Seasonality and Q2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 is softer for new CapEx due to monsoon; 100% utilisation with signed contracts for the full financial year.

risks_watch: Wind segment depends on 900-ton OEM supply (about 2-5 machines per month globally) and four-plus month lead times; no order book or revenue numbers disclosed yet.
UAE/KSA expansion relies on approvals, incorporation and client RFQs; management noted six-month demand halt in KSA and the paperwork delays; no CapEx quantum given.
Receivable days (~200 per analyst) versus management's 60-70 day target; watch next quarter's reported receivables.
Margin normalisation to 58-62% expected once OEM warranty ends, with 4-5% maintenance OpEx.
Quarterly revenue is 1.5-2 months of lag for newly commissioned machines; FY27 order book of INR 70-72 crore is small relative to the Q1 run-rate, so the disclosed figures need clarification.
Management declined FY28 estimates until December quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on demand, margins and expansion, with repeated claims of 100% utilisation. Evasive on FY28 numbers, wind segment economics, UAE/KSA CapEx size, and receivable reconciliation; several answers were loosely framed.
key_quotes: Total income increased by nearly 310% YoY to INR 1,680 lakhs, while EBITDA grew by approximately four times YoY to INR 1,087 lakhs.
We continue to maintain 100% fleet utilization, reflecting the strong demand environment and the efficient deployment of our equipment across multiple infrastructure projects.
The demand is not the issue. The supply is the issue.
Currently, we are at 65% margins. Eventually, it will drop down to 58-62%.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 growth backed by an executable order book of INR 70-72 crore covering the full year, 100% fleet utilisation, and ~INR 270 crore of INR 400 crore capex already done with INR 130-140 crore remaining (about 70% ordered), though no explicit FY27 revenue growth percentage was given and the wind and UAE/KSA plans lack signed orders or quantified capex.
